new_techniques.what: The native ComfyUI Wan Animate 2 template ships a WanAnimate2Cache node that caches pose computations across sampling steps, roughly halving generation time at the cost of extra system memory.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: A concrete, official speed lever for Animate-2 that has no analogue documented for Animate v1 in the skill.

new_techniques.what: Wan Animate 2's official template generates 81 frames (~3.4s@24fps) per pass; the documented way to extend past that is to duplicate the 'Motion Transfer' subgraph, wire its continue_motion/video_frame_offset outputs into the new copy, batch the IMAGE outputs, and trim the 1-frame overlap at each seam.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: This is the current official long-video-stitching recipe for character animation, replacing manual pose-extraction chaining used for Animate v1; a native looping PR (ComfyUI #13180) is still under review as the eventual replacement.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: references/motion-and-camera.md 'Animate' section, near any existing long-video-stitching guidance

new_techniques.what: Unlike Animate v1, Wan Animate 2 feeds raw driving-video frames directly into the DiT with no separate pose/keypoint extraction step, and decouples the output background/camera (text-controlled) from both the reference image and the driving video.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Removes a whole pipeline stage (pose extraction) that the skill's current Animate coverage assumes, and changes what the driving video is 'for' (motion only, not framing).

new_techniques.what: Alongside the base Wan-Animate-2-14B, Wan-AI ships a Wan2.2-Animate-2-14B-Distilled model for faster inference and, per Comfy's own coverage, a 'Lite' variant aimed at real-time streaming animation.
new_techniques.why_it_matters: Widens the Animate-2 variant selector beyond the single distilled checkpoint the existing open_finding already flags; the Lite/real-time angle is new and not covered anywhere.
new_techniques.where_it_belongs: SKILL.md task-mode selector 'Animate' row; references/motion-and-camera.md 'Animate' section
